subject: Partner request: SDK/endpoint migration, test hooks and deprecation cadence
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamline.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: remove legacy /v1/stream + SDK callback hook

Ben / Vanessa —

Quick note from our engineering team at Streamline. We’re planning a product release that relies on a lightweight event callback and a small change to how we call Redwood’s streaming endpoint. The legacy /v1/stream path currently returns a mixed payload that our SDK parses; we want to switch to the new /v2/events endpoint which separates event metadata from token frames.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood publish an official deprecation timeline for /v1/stream?
- Can the SDK add an opt-in compatibility flag so we can dual-run both endpoints while we validate?
- Could you provide a short test hook / canary window where Streamline can run our regression harness against the new endpoint?

This is moderately urgent for our roadmap — if we can get a 3–4 month runway to migrate clients it would be ideal. Attached is a short note from our eng lead that outlines traffic shape and the main parsing boundary we care about.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Head of Integrations, Streamline Analytics
Attachments: streamline-eng-note.pdf (summary), traffic-sample-202508.csv (sample)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamline.ai>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remove legacy /v1/stream + SDK callback hook

Tom —

Thanks for the heads up and the sample traffic. Sorry for the slightly delayed reply — I wanted to pull Karthik and Vanessa in so we can coordinate product + partner next steps.

High level: we can work with you on a migration that preserves customer experience, but we need to lock down the compatibility story and the deprecation window in writing. To move faster, I’ve attached a migration checklist we use for partners; it covers test hooks, canary windows, and docs updates.

Can you confirm:
- approx. % of your customers using the legacy parsing today (ballpark is fine)
- whether you can run an automated regression suite during a 2-week canary period

We’ll schedule a short sync. Proposing Wed 17 Sep or Thu 18 Sep for a 30-min technical alignment with Karthik and one of your eng leads.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: migration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamline.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remove legacy /v1/stream + SDK callback hook

Tom —

Thanks for the details. A few engineering notes and a proposed plan from our side: 

Summary of changes we’re proposing internally:
- Introduce /v2/events (structured event envelope + disaggregated token frames)
- Mark /v1/stream as deprecated but keep it operational during the migration window
- Publish OpenAPI diff and a compatibility flag in the next SDK patch (flag: client.useLegacyStream = true)

Proposed migration cadence (initial suggestion):
- Announcement + docs: week 0
- Canary: weeks 2–4 (2-week focused run + 2-week wider run)
- Deprecation effective: day 90 after announcement (90 days)
- Hard removal: 180 days after announcement for non-exempt partners

We can be flexible on the exact windows — for strategic partners we can extend the deprecation hard removal to 180 days. For the canary we’ll provide a test endpoint and a shared Drive folder with a regression harness. We’ll also add a small telemetry flag so partners can opt into debug traces for migration weeks.

Action items for Streamline:
- Share the regression harness output (logs) during canary
- Confirm percentage of live traffic you’ll route to /v2 during canary
- Run the attached checklist and flag any blocking regressions

Drive link to test harness and changelog: https://drive.redwood.local/Shared/Streamline/migration-harness

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Integrations (Redwood Inference)
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamline.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remove legacy /v1/stream + SDK callback hook

Karthik / team —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few notes from Streamline after internal sync: 
- 90 days will be very tight for our enterprise customers (many of whom are on quarterly change windows). We would request a 120-day deprecation/hard-removal at minimum, ideally with the option to request a 6-month exemption on a per-customer basis.
- The compatibility flag sounds perfect — do you plan to release the SDK patch as a minor or a major? We prefer a minor+feature-flag so we don’t trigger semver churn across our fleet.
- We can run the regression harness during the canary, but we need the canary to support full payload fidelity (headers + metadata).

If we can confirm: 1) compatibility flag in SDK as opt-in, 2) 120-day deprecation / 180-day hard removal for strategic partners, and 3) a 2-week closed canary then 4-week open canary, we can commit to a migration timeline and update our customers.

Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Integrations, Streamline Analytics
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamline.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2025 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remove legacy /v1/stream + SDK callback hook — alignment and next steps

Tom —

Thanks — we’re aligned with the requested adjustments and will adopt the following as the official partner migration plan for Streamline: 

Final agreed items:
- SDK: opt-in compatibility flag (client.useLegacyStream = true) released as a minor patch in the upcoming SDK cycle.
- Deprecation: public announcement + docs now; deprecation effective after 120 days from announcement.
- Hard removal: 180 days for standard partners; 6-month exemptions available on request for strategic customers (handle via partner ops).
- Canary: 2-week closed canary (internal + Streamline dev instances) followed by 4-week open canary for broader traffic.
- Test hooks: we will provide a full-fidelity canary endpoint and enable debug traces for your team.

Next steps:
- Ben will open a partner ops ticket to track exemptions and coordinate dates (HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/SL-2025-0482).
- Karthik will post the OpenAPI diff and the SDK feature-flag patch to the shared Drive by EOD Mon 22 Sep.
- Please run the migration-checklist.xlsx and post any blocking items to the shared folder.

We’ll schedule the technical sync for Wed 24 Sep at 10:00 PT — calendar invite forthcoming.

Thanks for working through this — we’ll make the process low-friction.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachments: openapi-diff.patch (unified diff)
